newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: FOCUS - Commerce cash call fuels merger tal.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Commerce cash call fuels merger tal.

text.p: A large cash call of 1.2 billion ringgit by Commerce Asset-Holding Bhd has fueled market speculation that its banking arm may soon announce merger talks with another banking group, analysts said on Thursday.

The bonus, rights, bond and special issues came after weeks of rumours that the well-connected financial group is keen to take a stake in the privatisation of Malaysia's second largest bank, Bank Bumiputra (Malaysia) Bhd.
The Malaysian government has announced that it plans to privatise Bank Bumiputra, possibly through a merger or a stock exchange listing.
"The announcement could mean that they (Commerce Asset) are looking at other acquisitions," said Pong Beng Swee, banking analyst at Vickers Ballas Research.
The cash call also raised eyebrows as Commerce Asset is already well capitalised and did not really need to raise a large amount of money for its organic growth.

"The (Commerce Asset) cash call is too big for just normal expansion," said ING-Barings Research banking analyst, Soon Teck Onn. "They are doubling their capital base. It's definitely something else."

Analysts said if not Bank Bumiputra, Commerce Asset may have other banks which it plans to acquire. The government has called for banks to merge in order to better compete in the coming era of financial liberalisation. Malaysia has some 37 banks serving a population of only 20 million.
"Commerce has a bank merger plan in its current five-year plan," said an analyst at a Malaysian stockbrokerage house.
Commerce Asset's executive director Rozali Mohamed Ali told reporters the proposed issues were aimed at increasing working capital and to finance the group's expansion.
But he declined to be more specific.
"We are not making public the provisions we are making," Rozali said. "We'll expand our operations either through internal growth or acquisitions."
Under the proposed plan announced on Thursday, Commerce Asset said it wants to raise its authorised share capital from 500 million ringgit to one billion.
The company said in a statement it was planning a one-for-one bonus issue totalling 319.16 million shares.
This would be followed by a special issue of 9.034 million shares at 6.50 ringgit a share for Bumiputera (ethnic Malay) investors.
On completion of the bonus and special issues, Commerce Asset plans to carry out a one-for-five rights issue of 129.47 million shares at 6.50 ringgit a share.
The company also plans to issue five-year zero coupon bonds to raise 400 million ringgit with 80.92 million detachable warrants, the statement said.
Commerce Asset's banking arm, Bank of Commerce (Malaysia) Bhd, is rated the sixth largest in Malaysia in terms of assets.
Analysts said with the central bank spurring more mergers between local banks, a marriage between Bank of Commerce and Bank Bumiputra is not unlikely.
Market interest on bank mergers has been heightened by a recent 2.6 billion ringgit deal involving the planned merger of Kwong Yik Bank Bhd and DCB Holdings Bhd's DCB Bank Bhd.
